question.problem:
Compute $P(X\le -4)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}},\, & x\le -1, \\ 0,\, & x>-1.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le -4) & =P(-\infty <X\le -4) \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{-4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{-4}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}]}_{-\infty }^{-4} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
